candidates.name: Narukiyo
candidates.reason: Kitchen-facing seating is a standing-style counter (per its Tabelog listing), unsuited to a seated 6-person dinner; its Tabelog EN page and Time Out Tokyo coverage show it is already surfaced in English-language tourist guides, undermining the under-the-radar/local angle this pass exists to find; Tabelog also showed the phone reservation line closed at time of research, adding booking friction on top.

candidates.name: Kagayaki
candidates.reason: All-you-can-eat yakiniku/shabu-shabu buffet format — a value/quantity pick, not the quality-led anchor experience the trip's food priority calls for; better suited to a casual, low-friction meal than the deliberate Saturday anchor. Only surface-level discovery (blog + aggregator listings, no primary/operator fetch) before being dropped in favor of stronger finds.

candidates.name: Miyabi
candidates.reason: Surfaced from a single note.com blog only; a generic high-end Roppongi tourist-district yakiniku/French-fusion spot without a distinct local angle. Dropped once Kobikicho Ohno and Koumoto (native-only-discoverable, room capacity confirmed to fit a party of 6) proved stronger, better-corroborated picks.

candidates.name: Kaigen
candidates.reason: Genuinely appealing insider tuna-bowl pick inside Tsukiji Outer Market (professional-grade tuna via the Yamakoh wholesaler; arrive ~9:20am for first seating to beat the queue) — but only ONE current (≤24-month) independent firsthand account exists (asanoyoko.com, Sept 2025). The other two corroborating accounts found (shamo-rock.com, 4travel.jp) date to 2022, past the 24-month experiential-freshness bar, so the ≥2-recent-independent-source bar isn't cleared within this pass's budget. Worth re-checking with a fresh search in a later pass rather than shipping on stale corroboration.

evidence.claim: Kobikicho Ohno (木挽町 大野), a tea-kaiseki restaurant in Yotsuya-sanchome, accepts only one reservation/party per day — the entire restaurant serves a single seating.

Official site lists dinner hours 17:00–21:00 (drinks last order 20:00), with no fixed weekly closure day but irregular ad-hoc closures ('定休日なし（不定休日あり）'); Saturday hours are not separately differentiated on the site, so confirm directly for a specific date.
The restaurant's only private room (horigotatsu sunken-hearth, with door and walls) seats 2–6 guests — a party of 6 fills it exactly, with no overflow buffer for a 7th guest.
≈¥15,000 per person average budget for dinner, per Gurunavi's operator listing (the restaurant's own official site does not publish a fixed course price).
Cancellation fee tiers per Gurunavi's operator listing: 50% fee inside 7 days of the reservation date, full charge inside 3 days.

Official site states an English-language menu and English-speaking staff are available; card acceptance is not mentioned on the official site or the Gurunavi operator page — unconfirmed, ask when booking.
Koumoto (こうもと), a soba-kappo restaurant in Nishi-Azabu/Minami-Azabu, is open Saturdays 17:00–22:00 (food last order 21:00, drinks last order 21:30), per its HotPepper Gourmet operator page.
Two 2nd-floor private rooms (seating 2–4 and 3–8) plus additional 3rd-floor rooms, combinable up to 12 guests — comfortably fits a party of 6 with spare capacity, unlike Ohno's exact-fit room.
≈¥10,000 per person starting price for dinner courses, plus a 10% service charge, per HotPepper's operator listing.
Accepts Visa, Mastercard, Diners Club, and JCB — confirmed foreign-card compatibility, stronger than Kobikicho Ohno's (unconfirmed).

Tsukiji Outer Market is markedly less crowded in the early morning (roughly before 9:00–9:30am) and crowding concentrates in specific hotspot areas rather than across the whole market; Wednesdays and Sundays see reduced stall operations (only about half the shops open).

reservations.actionDate: Contact as early as practical for Sat 2026-10-17 (phone 050-5486-6483 or the official site) — the single-seating-per-day format makes the date itself, not a release window, the real constraint.

reservations.fallback: If Ohno cannot be secured for 2026-10-17, book Koumoto or another private-room kaiseki/kappo house in the same window rather than defaulting to a walk-in-friendly but lower-quality option, per the intake's priority on food quality over convenience.

transport.notApplicableReason: This pass researched Food & Dining only; no route reached R3+ risk — routine Tokyo train/subway transfers to these central-Tokyo restaurants are the forgiving default and weren't researched to transport-robustness depth here.

saturation.note: After roughly 19 web searches and 8 fetches, native-language searches for anchor-dinner-caliber restaurants with 6-person private rooms converged on two genuinely non-default candidates (Kobikicho Ohno, Koumoto); further searches for individual venue write-ups kept returning the same aggregator round-ups (ikyu.com, hitosara.com, Retty) rather than new venues. The one open thread — Ohno's exact Saturday 2026-10-17 availability — is a booking-logistics detail to resolve by direct contact, not a discovery gap that would change which venue to recommend, so it doesn't block stopping.

nativeLanguage.why: English/generic search results for 'Tokyo restaurant for 6' or 'best Tokyo izakaya' are dominated by SEO round-ups (ikyu.com, hitosara.com, Retty, Tabelog matome pages) and don't surface exclusive, reservation-hard venues. Japanese queries built around reservation-difficulty and room-capacity vocabulary (予約困難, 個室6名, 隠れ家, 一軒家) reached restaurants with little to no English coverage, matching the anti-default charter; yt-dlp is not installed in this environment, so the video-transcript lead channel was skipped per the bot-blocked doctrine and did not block the pass.

nativeLanguage.yield: Surfaced two non-default anchor-dinner candidates confirmed (via fetched operator/official sources) to fit a party of 6 in a private room: Kobikicho Ohno (one-party-per-day tea-kaiseki, exact 6-seat room) and Koumoto (soba-kappo, private rooms to 8, confirmed card acceptance). Corroborated Tsukiji Outer Market's early-morning off-peak window from two independent firsthand blogs. Identified and rejected three candidates that looked promising but didn't clear the bar: Narukiyo (standing-counter format wrong for a seated 6-top, and already English-tourist-discovered), Kagayaki (all-you-can-eat format mismatched to the quality-first brief), and Kaigen (appealing insider tuna-bowl pick, but its only current firsthand corroboration is a single 2025 source — the other two are 2022, past the 24-month freshness bar).
